summary: The change replaces a misleading JSON error and preserves HTTP status internally with little added complexity. User-facing commands still omit that status; live rate-limit benefit and incident frequency remain unknown.
reasons: The fix addresses the reported parsing mistake with limited maintenance cost: one failure branch, existing error handling, and focused tests.
The intended audience still cannot distinguish rate limiting from other lookup failures. HTTP status survives internally, but the command outputs expose only error messages.
The packet reports a passing reproduction and full validation. Live rate-limit behavior and incident frequency remain unknown.
Review required one round with no repairs. The earlier exit-8 coverage finding is a test nit, not a substantive product concern. No instruction changes require an instruction-growth assessment.
concerns: skills/shaka/lib/shaka/github/check_list.rb replaces the invalid-JSON message with a generic gh failure and preserves HTTP status only as metadata. scripts/shaka.rb and pr_watch/command.rb print e.message; status.rb stores only e.message in requiredChecksUnavailable. Agents and maintainers therefore still receive no HTTP status or rate-limit diagnosis through the named commands, leaving the central user outcome incomplete.
alternative: Keep the bounded fix and expose the parsed HTTP status in the existing safe error message, including the required-check wrapper. Preserve stderr exclusion and existing failure safeguards; no new configuration or error framework is needed.
next_action: Revise this PR to include the parsed HTTP status in check-failure messages and verify that the existing command outputs retain it.
